title: Equivariant marked nodal reduction of a single relative curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $Y$ be a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $C$ be an integral proper finite-type $k$-scheme with a proper dominant morphism $g:C\to Y$ whose generic fibre is a geometrically integral curve. Let a finite group $H$ act compatibly on $k,C,Y,g$, and let $E\subset C$ be an $H$-stable nowhere dense closed subset. There exist a finite extension $e/k$, a finite group $G$ with a surjection $\alpha:G\to H$, compatible $G$-actions on $e,B,V$, a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $e$-scheme $B$, and a commutative square $gc=bv$ with $c:V\to C$, $b:B\to Y$ H-projective surjective alterations and $v:V\to B$ H-projective, flat and finitely presented. An alteration means a proper surjective morphism between integral schemes inducing a finite extension of function fields and finite over a dense open of the target. Both horizontal maps are equivariant via $\alpha$; the action on $e$ extends the action on $k$. Put $A=\ker\alpha$. Then $e^A/k$, $k(B)^A/k(Y)$ and $k(V)^A/k(C)$ are purely inseparable extensions.

Every geometric fibre of $v$ is a nonempty connected reduced curve of pure dimension one with at most ordinary double points; an ordinary double point has completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[u,w]]/(uw)$. The generic fibre is smooth and geometrically integral. There are finitely many disjoint sections $s_j:B\to V$ in the relative smooth locus whose union is $G$-stable, and a $G$-stable nowhere dense closed subset $D\subset B$, such that $v$ is smooth over $B\setminus D$ and $c^{-1}E\subseteq v^{-1}D\cup\bigcup_j s_j(B)$. The curve is quasi-split: for every point $t\in B$, all singular points of $V_t$ and the two points over each of them in its normalization are rational over $\kappa(t)$. The group may permute the sections and the fibre graphs. These projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, geometric-fibre, quasi-split and section properties persist under arbitrary base change. If $\dim Y=0$, then $B=\operatorname{Spec}e$ and $D=\varnothing$.

Field, integrality, properness, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, H-projectivity, finite morphisms, surjectivity and function fields use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and [def-sc-function-field]. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Finite extensions and purely inseparable extensions use [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, sections and base change use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-pc-fibre-product]. Normalization, completion and the formal power series notation use [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

proof.text: Put $K=k(Y)$ and $F=k(C)$. Apply equivariant flat preparation to $(g,H,E)$, obtaining $S,P,f,M,a,b_0$ with $K_0=k(S)/K$ finite purely inseparable. Put $F_0=k(P)=F\otimes_K K_0$. The generic curve of $P/S$ is smooth geometrically integral and its reduced generic marking is finite etale. The $H$-action is retained. Fields are excellent, finite-type algebras and their localizations are excellent, and finite-type schemes over a field are Noetherian; hence all bases constructed below are excellent Noetherian. This step prepares the generic curve and the target, and makes no stable-modification claim.

Apply genus-raising-equivariant-stable-model to $P/S,M,H$. Retain its $Q/S_1,H_1,S_2,H_2,(W,s_i)$ and generic identification. Write $K_i=k(S_i)$ and $F_1=k(Q)$. Its fixed-field equalities give $F_1^{\ker(H_1\to H)}=F_0$, $K_1^{\ker(H_1\to H)}=K_0$, and $K_2^{\ker(H_2\to H_1)}=K_1$.

source.place: §§3.2--3.8, pp.605--609; returned proof Steps 2--4, including genus raising, rational markings, stable extension, Isom rigidity and projective-bundle conversion.

proof.text: Apply equivariant-stable-model-evaluation to $W/S_2$, $Q\times_{S_1}S_2$ and the generic identification. The no-rational-curve hypothesis follows from the preceding cover on geometric fibres. Obtain $S_3,H_3,W_3$ and an equivariant map $W_3\to Q\to P\to C$. The lemma supplies integrality after every subsequent dominant integral base change and the finite-extension tensor description of its function field.

source.place: §§3.9--3.13, p.609; returned proof Steps 5--6, including equivariant normal domination of Hom closure and flat generic-field calculation.

proof.text: Apply curve-field-kernel-invariant-tower first to $F_1/K_1$ and $K_2/K_1$, then to $k(W)/K_2$ and $k(S_3)/K_2$. Geometric integrality supplies its tensor-domain hypothesis. The equivariant generic identification of genus-raising-equivariant-stable-model gives $k(W)=F_1\otimes_{K_1}K_2$ with the diagonal $H_2$-action. The evaluation lemma supplies the second tensor identification and kernel base-field equality. Starting with $F_0/F$ and $K_0/K$ purely inseparable, the tower conclusion gives $k(W_3)^{A_3}/F$ and $k(S_3)^{A_3}/K$ purely inseparable, where $A_3=\ker(H_3\to H)$.

source.place: Remarks 2.3(iii), §2.6 and §§3.2,3.5,3.11; returned proof Steps 7--8, tensor fixed fields and characteristic powers. Agent-expanded field algebra.

proof.text: Use quasisplit-regular-constant-alteration with $S=S_3,W=W_3$, its equivariant evaluation to $C$ and the preceding invariant fields. Evaluation is dominant and generically finite by its generic identification and the finite auxiliary cover. The base map $S_3\to Y$ is a composite of alterations, hence an alteration; the lemma asks for no H-projectivity of it. Obtain $e,G,B,V,v,b,c,\alpha$ with all three kernel-invariant conclusions, H-projective alterations, stable markings, quasi-split fibres, and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. If $\dim Y=0$, it gives $B=\operatorname{Spec}e$.

source.place: Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, pp.614--615, and §3.11; returned proof Steps 9--11, finite quasi-splitting, radicial constants and H-projective graph alterations.

proof.text: Set $Z=c^{-1}E$. The generic identification and the genus-raising cover identify its reduced generic inverse image with marked points. Apply marked-nodal-boundary-control to obtain the invariant nowhere dense $D$, smoothness off $D$ and the required containment. The same lemma gives all asserted arbitrary-base-change properties and, when $B=\operatorname{Spec}e$, $D=\varnothing$. Together these data satisfy every clause of the unchanged statement.

source.place: Remark 2.5, p.603, §§3.3,5.5--5.7; returned proof Steps 12--13, exceptional boundary images, arbitrary base change and dimension-zero case.

The item statement is byte-identical to live and the parent is a 6-step assembly (2698 characters, 2920 after the fixes). Each node is true when checked against its cited existing nodes. Genus-raising: high-genus cover, then stable-pointed generic extension, then separable domination giving K_2^{N_2}=K_1, then Isom-finite uniqueness for the H_2 action, then projective-bundle→H-projective. Evaluation: Hom closure, equivariant domination of R (separable, so (L')^N=L), and flat torsion-free integrality with D⊗L_T a field. Field tower: N acts trivially on L, so (D_M⊗_M L')^N=D_M by tensor invariants; A'→A is surjective, so p-powers propagate along kernels. Quasisplit: quasi-splitting, then constant regularization, then the graph H-projective argument; V integral is advisory because the old Step-6 argument must be redone there. Boundary: dominating components of Z lie in the closed sections; other images and the nonsmooth image are proper closed subsets; dim 0 gives D=∅; base-change persistence holds. Small cases checked: char 0, empty marking, nonfaithful or trivial actions, dim 0. de Jong 1997 has no local PDF (already WANTED on base); the places given (Thm 2.4/Rem 2.5, §3.2–3.13, Lemmas 5.5/5.7) match the paper's structure. The hypothesis is redundant (graph argument: S projective over k, Y separated), so I deleted 'H-projective' from it in the new node and Step 5 now says the base map is an alteration.
